passages.text: Now the word of the LORD came to me, saying, “Go and proclaim in the hearing of Jerusalem that this is what the LORD says: ‘I remember the devotion of your youth, your love as a bride, how you followed Me in the wilderness, in a land not sown.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to me.
He gave me a message.
He told me to go to Jerusalem.
He told me to speak to the people there.
He told me to say, “This is what the LORD says.”
The LORD remembers Jerusalem’s early devotion.
He remembers their love when they were like a young bride.
He remembers how they followed Him in the wilderness.
They followed Him in a land that was not planted.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר־ יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר׃ הָלֹ֡ךְ וְקָֽרָאתָ֩ בְאָזְנֵ֨י יְרוּשָׁלִַ֜ם לֵאמֹ֗ר כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה זָכַ֤רְתִּי לָךְ֙ חֶ֣סֶד נְעוּרַ֔יִךְ אַהֲבַ֖ת כְּלוּלֹתָ֑יִךְ לֶכְתֵּ֤ךְ אַחֲרַי֙ בַּמִּדְבָּ֔ר בְּאֶ֖רֶץ לֹ֥א זְרוּעָֽה׃

passages.text: Israel was holy to the LORD, the firstfruits of His harvest. All who devoured her found themselves guilty; disaster came upon them,’ ” declares the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The LORD chose Israel.
Israel belonged to the LORD.
Israel was holy to the LORD.
Israel was the first part of the LORD’s harvest.
Anyone who attacked Israel became guilty.
Disaster came to those people.
The LORD said these things.
passages.original: קֹ֤דֶשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ לַיהוָ֔ה רֵאשִׁ֖ית תְּבוּאָתֹ֑ה כָּל־ אֹכְלָ֣יו יֶאְשָׁ֔מוּ רָעָ֛ה תָּבֹ֥א אֲלֵיהֶ֖ם נְאֻם־ יְהוָֽה׃פ

passages.text: Hear the word of the LORD, O house of Jacob, and all you families of the house of Israel.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks to the people of Israel.
The LORD addresses the house of Jacob.
The LORD calls to all the families of Israel.
The LORD commands them to listen to His word.
The LORD says, "Hear My word, house of Jacob.
Hear My word, all families of Israel."
passages.original: שִׁמְע֥וּ דְבַר־ יְהוָ֖ה בֵּ֣ית יַעֲקֹ֑ב וְכָֽל־ מִשְׁפְּח֖וֹת בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: This is what the LORD says: “What fault did your fathers find in Me that they strayed so far from Me, and followed worthless idols, and became worthless themselves?
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks to Israel.
The LORD asks a question.
The LORD says, “What wrong did your fathers find in Me?
Why did your fathers turn away from Me?
Your fathers went far from Me.
Your fathers followed worthless idols.
Your fathers became worthless like those idols.”
passages.original: כֹּ֣ה׀ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה מַה־ מָּצְא֨וּ אֲבוֹתֵיכֶ֥ם בִּי֙ עָ֔וֶל כִּ֥י רָחֲק֖וּ מֵעָלָ֑י וַיֵּֽלְכ֛וּ אַחֲרֵ֥י הַהֶ֖בֶל וַיֶּהְבָּֽלוּ׃

passages.text: They did not ask, ‘Where is the LORD who brought us up from the land of Egypt, who led us through the wilderness, through a land of deserts and pits, a land of drought and darkness, a land where no one travels and no one lives?’
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel did not ask about the LORD.
The LORD brought their ancestors out of Egypt.
The LORD led them through the wilderness.
The wilderness was a land of deserts and pits.
It was a land of drought and darkness.
No one traveled in that land.
No one lived there.
The people did not say, "Where is the LORD who did these things for us?"
passages.original: וְלֹ֣א אָמְר֔וּ אַיֵּ֣ה יְהוָ֔ה הַמַּעֲלֶ֥ה אֹתָ֖נוּ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם הַמּוֹלִ֨יךְ אֹתָ֜נוּ בַּמִּדְבָּ֗ר בְּאֶ֨רֶץ עֲרָבָ֤ה וְשׁוּחָה֙ בְּאֶ֙רֶץ֙ צִיָּ֣ה וְצַלְמָ֔וֶת בְּאֶ֗רֶץ לֹֽא־ עָ֤בַר בָּהּ֙ אִ֔ישׁ וְלֹֽא־ יָשַׁ֥ב אָדָ֖ם שָֽׁם׃

passages.text: I brought you into a fertile land to eat its fruit and bounty, but you came and defiled My land, and made My inheritance detestable.
passages.sermon:
The LORD brought the people of Israel into a fertile land.
He gave them this land so they could eat its fruit.
He gave them this land so they could enjoy its bounty.
The people of Israel entered the land.
They defiled the LORD’s land.
They made the LORD’s inheritance detestable.
passages.original: וָאָבִ֤יא אֶתְכֶם֙ אֶל־ אֶ֣רֶץ הַכַּרְמֶ֔ל לֶאֱכֹ֥ל פִּרְיָ֖הּ וְטוּבָ֑הּ וַתָּבֹ֙אוּ֙ וַתְּטַמְּא֣וּ אֶת־ אַרְצִ֔י וְנַחֲלָתִ֥י שַׂמְתֶּ֖ם לְתוֹעֵבָֽה׃

passages.text: The priests did not ask, ‘Where is the LORD?’ The experts in the law no longer knew Me, and the leaders rebelled against Me. The prophets prophesied by Baal and followed useless idols.
passages.sermon:
The priests did not ask about the LORD.
The priests did not say, "Where is the LORD?"
The experts in the law did not know God.
The leaders rebelled against God.
The prophets spoke messages in the name of Baal.
The prophets followed idols that cannot help.
passages.original: הַכֹּהֲנִ֗ים לֹ֤א אָֽמְרוּ֙ אַיֵּ֣ה יְהוָ֔ה וְתֹפְשֵׂ֤י הַתּוֹרָה֙ לֹ֣א יְדָע֔וּנִי וְהָרֹעִ֖ים פָּ֣שְׁעוּ בִ֑י וְהַנְּבִיאִים֙ נִבְּא֣וּ בַבַּ֔עַל וְאַחֲרֵ֥י לֹֽא־ יוֹעִ֖לוּ הָלָֽכוּ׃

passages.text: Therefore, I will contend with you again, declares the LORD, and I will bring a case against your children’s children.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks to His people.
The LORD says, “I will argue with you again.
I will bring charges against you.
I will also bring charges against your grandchildren.
I, the LORD, declare this.”
passages.original: לָכֵ֗ן עֹ֛ד אָרִ֥יב אִתְּכֶ֖ם נְאֻם־ יְהוָ֑ה וְאֶת־ בְּנֵ֥י בְנֵיכֶ֖ם אָרִֽיב׃

passages.text: Cross over to the coasts of Cyprus and take a look; send to Kedar and consider carefully; see if there has ever been anything like this: Has a nation ever changed its gods, though they are no gods at all? Yet My people have exchanged their Glory for useless idols.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Israel.
God tells the people to look at other nations.
God says, “Go to the coasts of Cyprus.
Look there.
Send messengers to Kedar.
Think about what you see very carefully.
Ask if anything like this has ever happened before.
Has any nation ever changed its gods?
Those gods are not real gods.
But My people have done something worse.
My people have traded their Glory.
They have given up the true God.
They have chosen useless idols instead.”
passages.original: כִּ֣י עִבְר֞וּ אִיֵּ֤י כִתִּיִּים֙ וּרְא֔וּ וְקֵדָ֛ר שִׁלְח֥וּ וְהִֽתְבּוֹנְנ֖וּ מְאֹ֑ד וּרְא֕וּ הֵ֥ן הָיְתָ֖ה כָּזֹֽאת׃ הַהֵימִ֥יר גּוֹי֙ אֱלֹהִ֔ים וְהֵ֖מָּה לֹ֣א אֱלֹהִ֑ים וְעַמִּ֛י הֵמִ֥יר כְּבוֹד֖וֹ בְּל֥וֹא יוֹעִֽיל׃

passages.text: Be stunned by this, O heavens; be shocked and utterly appalled,” declares the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks.
The LORD commands the heavens.
The LORD says, “Heavens, be stunned by this.
Heavens, be shocked.
Heavens, be utterly appalled.”
passages.original: שֹׁ֥מּוּ שָׁמַ֖יִם עַל־ זֹ֑את וְשַׂעֲר֛וּ חָרְב֥וּ מְאֹ֖ד נְאֻם־ יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: “For My people have committed two evils: They have forsaken Me, the fountain of living water, and they have dug their own cisterns— broken cisterns that cannot hold water.
passages.sermon:
God speaks about His people Israel.
God says His people have done two evil things.
First, they have left God.
God is the source of living water.
Second, they have made their own cisterns.
These cisterns are broken.
The broken cisterns cannot hold water.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ שְׁתַּ֥יִם רָע֖וֹת עָשָׂ֣ה עַמִּ֑י אֹתִ֨י עָזְב֜וּ מְק֣וֹר׀ מַ֣יִם חַיִּ֗ים לַחְצֹ֤ב לָהֶם֙ בֹּאר֔וֹת בֹּארֹת֙ נִשְׁבָּרִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹא־ יָכִ֖לוּ הַמָּֽיִם׃

passages.text: Is Israel a slave? Was he born into slavery? Why then has he become prey?
passages.sermon:
Israel is God's chosen people.
Israel is not a slave.
Israel was not born into slavery.
Why has Israel become prey?
passages.original: הַעֶ֙בֶד֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אִם־ יְלִ֥יד בַּ֖יִת ה֑וּא מַדּ֖וּעַ הָיָ֥ה לָבַֽז׃

passages.text: The young lions have roared at him; they have growled with a loud voice. They have laid waste his land; his cities lie in ruins, without inhabitant.
passages.sermon:
Young lions attacked Israel.
They roared at him with loud voices.
They destroyed his land.
His cities are burned.
No one lives in them.
passages.original: עָלָיו֙ יִשְׁאֲג֣וּ כְפִרִ֔ים נָתְנ֖וּ קוֹלָ֑ם וַיָּשִׁ֤יתוּ אַרְצוֹ֙ לְשַׁמָּ֔ה עָרָ֥יו נִצְּתָה מִבְּלִ֥י יֹשֵֽׁב׃

passages.text: The men of Memphis and Tahpanhes have shaved the crown of your head.
passages.sermon:
The men of Memphis have acted against you.
The men of Tahpanhes have acted against you.
They have shaved the crown of your head.
They have brought you shame.
You have suffered humiliation from foreign people.
passages.original: גַּם־ בְּנֵי־ נֹ֖ף וְתַחְפְּנֵס יִרְע֖וּךְ קָדְקֹֽד׃

passages.text: Have you not brought this on yourself by forsaking the LORD your God when He led you in the way?
passages.sermon:
You have brought this trouble on yourself.
You turned away from the LORD your God.
The LORD your God was leading you in the right way.
You chose to leave Him.
That is why you suffer now.
passages.original: הֲלוֹא־ זֹ֖את תַּעֲשֶׂה־ לָּ֑ךְ עָזְבֵךְ֙ אֶת־ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהַ֔יִךְ בְּעֵ֖ת מוֹלִיכֵ֥ךְ בַּדָּֽרֶךְ׃

passages.text: Now what will you gain on your way to Egypt to drink the waters of the Nile ? What will you gain on your way to Assyria to drink the waters of the Euphrates ?
passages.sermon:
God speaks to His people.
God asks a question.
He says, “Why do you go to Egypt?
Why do you travel that road?
Do you go to drink the waters of the Nile?
Why do you go to Assyria?
Why do you travel that road?
Do you go to drink the waters of the Euphrates?
What do you gain by doing this?”
passages.original: וְעַתָּ֗ה מַה־ לָּךְ֙ לְדֶ֣רֶךְ מִצְרַ֔יִם לִשְׁתּ֖וֹת מֵ֣י שִׁח֑וֹר וּמַה־ לָּךְ֙ לְדֶ֣רֶךְ אַשּׁ֔וּר לִשְׁתּ֖וֹת מֵ֥י נָהָֽר׃

passages.text: Your own evil will discipline you; your own apostasies will reprimand you. Consider and realize how evil and bitter it is for you to forsake the LORD your God and to have no fear of Me,” declares the Lord GOD of Hosts.
passages.sermon:
The Lord GOD of Hosts speaks.
He says this to His people.
Your own evil actions will discipline you.
Your own turning away will correct you.
See and understand this.
It is evil and bitter for you to leave the LORD your God.
You do not fear Me.
This is what the Lord GOD of Hosts declares.
passages.original: תְּיַסְּרֵ֣ךְ רָעָתֵ֗ךְ וּמְשֻֽׁבוֹתַ֙יִךְ֙ תּוֹכִחֻ֔ךְ וּדְעִ֤י וּרְאִי֙ כִּי־ רַ֣ע וָמָ֔ר עָזְבֵ֖ךְ אֶת־ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהָ֑יִךְ וְלֹ֤א פַחְדָּתִי֙ אֵלַ֔יִךְ נְאֻם־ אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֖ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃

passages.text: “For long ago you broke your yoke and tore off your chains, saying, ‘I will not serve!’ Indeed, on every high hill and under every green tree you lay down as a prostitute.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to His people Israel.
God says He freed Israel long ago.
God broke Israel’s yoke.
God tore off Israel’s chains.
Israel said, “I will not serve.”
Israel refused to obey God.
Israel went to every high hill.
Israel went under every green tree.
Israel acted like a prostitute there.
passages.original: כִּ֣י מֵעוֹלָ֞ם שָׁבַ֣רְתִּי עֻלֵּ֗ךְ נִתַּ֙קְתִּי֙ מוֹסְרֹתַ֔יִךְ וַתֹּאמְרִ֖י לֹ֣א אֶעֱבֹד כִּ֣י עַֽל־ כָּל־ גִּבְעָ֞ה גְּבֹהָ֗ה וְתַ֙חַת֙ כָּל־ עֵ֣ץ רַעֲנָ֔ן אַ֖תְּ צֹעָ֥ה זֹנָֽה׃

passages.text: I had planted you like a choice vine from the very best seed. How could you turn yourself before Me into a rotten, wild vine?
passages.sermon:
God speaks to His people.
God says, "I planted you like a special vine.
I chose the best seed for you.
You were meant to be true and good.
But you changed completely.
You became a wild and foreign vine.
You turned bad in My sight."
passages.original: וְאָֽנֹכִי֙ נְטַעְתִּ֣יךְ שֹׂרֵ֔ק כֻּלֹּ֖ה זֶ֣רַע אֱמֶ֑ת וְאֵיךְ֙ נֶהְפַּ֣כְתְּ לִ֔י סוּרֵ֖י הַגֶּ֥פֶן נָכְרִיָּֽה׃

passages.text: Although you wash with lye and use an abundance of soap, the stain of your guilt is still before Me,” declares the Lord GOD.
passages.sermon:
The Lord GOD speaks.
He sees the people’s guilt.
He says, “You try to wash yourself clean.
You use lye.
You use much soap.
But your guilt remains before Me.
You cannot remove your sin from My sight.”
passages.original: כִּ֤י אִם־ תְּכַבְּסִי֙ בַּנֶּ֔תֶר וְתַרְבִּי־ לָ֖ךְ בֹּרִ֑ית נִכְתָּ֤ם עֲוֺנֵךְ֙ לְפָנַ֔י נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה׃

passages.text: “How can you say, ‘I am not defiled; I have not run after the Baals’? Look at your behavior in the valley; acknowledge what you have done. You are a swift young she-camel galloping here and there, a wild donkey at home in the wilderness, sniffing the wind in the heat of her desire. Who can restrain her passion? All who seek her need not weary themselves; in mating season they will find her.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Israel.
Israel claims, “I am not defiled.”
Israel says, “I have not followed the Baals.”
God tells Israel, “Look at your actions in the valley.”
God commands, “Recognize what you have done.”
Israel acts like a young she-camel.
The she-camel runs quickly in many directions.
Israel is also like a wild donkey.
The wild donkey lives in the wilderness.
The donkey sniffs the wind when she desires a mate.
No one can restrain her passion.
Anyone who seeks her does not grow tired.
In her mating season, they will find her easily.
passages.original: אֵ֣יךְ תֹּאמְרִ֞י לֹ֣א נִטְמֵ֗אתִי אַחֲרֵ֤י הַבְּעָלִים֙ לֹ֣א הָלַ֔כְתִּי רְאִ֤י דַרְכֵּךְ֙ בַּגַּ֔יְא דְּעִ֖י מֶ֣ה עָשִׂ֑ית בִּכְרָ֥ה קַלָּ֖ה מְשָׂרֶ֥כֶת דְּרָכֶֽיהָ׃ פֶּ֣רֶה׀ לִמֻּ֣ד מִדְבָּ֗ר בְּאַוַּ֤ת נַפְשׁוֹ שָׁאֲפָ֣ה ר֔וּחַ תַּאֲנָתָ֖הּ מִ֣י יְשִׁיבֶ֑נָּה כָּל־ מְבַקְשֶׁ֙יהָ֙ לֹ֣א יִיעָ֔פוּ בְּחָדְשָׁ֖הּ יִמְצָאֽוּנְהָ׃

passages.text: You should have kept your feet from going bare and your throat from being thirsty. But you said, ‘It is hopeless! For I love foreign gods, and I must go after them.’
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the people of Judah.
God tells them what they should have done.
You should have protected your feet from going bare.
You should have kept your throat from being thirsty.
But you did not listen.
You said, “It is hopeless.”
You said, “No, I love foreign gods.”
You said, “I must go after them.”
passages.original: מִנְעִ֤י רַגְלֵךְ֙ מִיָּחֵ֔ף וְגוֹרְנֵךְ מִצִּמְאָ֑ה וַתֹּאמְרִ֣י נוֹאָ֔שׁ ל֕וֹא כִּֽי־ אָהַ֥בְתִּי זָרִ֖ים וְאַחֲרֵיהֶ֥ם אֵלֵֽךְ׃

passages.text: As the thief is ashamed when he is caught, so the house of Israel is disgraced. They, their kings, their officials, their priests, and their prophets say to a tree, ‘You are my father,’ and to a stone, ‘You gave me birth.’ For they have turned their backs to Me and not their faces, yet in the time of trouble they beg, ‘Rise up and save us!’
passages.sermon:
The house of Israel feels deep shame.
They are like a thief who is caught.
Their kings feel shame.
Their officials feel shame.
Their priests feel shame.
Their prophets feel shame.
They speak to a tree and say, “You are my father.”
They speak to a stone and say, “You gave me birth.”
They have turned their backs to God.
They do not turn their faces to God.
When they are in trouble, they call out to God.
They say, “Rise up and save us!”
passages.original: כְּבֹ֤שֶׁת גַּנָּב֙ כִּ֣י יִמָּצֵ֔א כֵּ֥ן הֹבִ֖ישׁוּ בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל הֵ֤מָּה מַלְכֵיהֶם֙ שָֽׂרֵיהֶ֔ם וְכֹהֲנֵיהֶ֖ם וּנְבִיאֵיהֶֽם׃ אֹמְרִ֨ים לָעֵ֜ץ אָ֣בִי אַ֗תָּה וְלָאֶ֙בֶן֙ אַ֣תְּ יְלִדְתִּנִי כִּֽי־ פָנ֥וּ אֵלַ֛י עֹ֖רֶף וְלֹ֣א פָנִ֑ים וּבְעֵ֤ת רָֽעָתָם֙ יֹֽאמְר֔וּ ק֖וּמָה וְהוֹשִׁיעֵֽנוּ׃

passages.text: But where are the gods you made for yourselves? Let them rise up in your time of trouble and save you if they can; for your gods are as numerous as your cities, O Judah.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the people of Judah.
Judah has made many false gods for themselves.
Judah has as many gods as they have cities.
God asks, "Where are the gods you made for yourselves?"
God says, "Let your gods rise up in your time of trouble."
God says, "Let them save you if they can."
passages.original: וְאַיֵּ֤ה אֱלֹהֶ֙יךָ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשִׂ֣יתָ לָּ֔ךְ יָק֕וּמוּ אִם־ יוֹשִׁיע֖וּךָ בְּעֵ֣ת רָעָתֶ֑ךָ כִּ֚י מִסְפַּ֣ר עָרֶ֔יךָ הָי֥וּ אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ יְהוּדָֽה׃ס

passages.text: Why do you bring a case against Me? You have all rebelled against Me,” declares the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks to the people of Israel.
The LORD asks, "Why do you argue with Me?"
All of you have rebelled against Me.
This is the declaration of the LORD.
passages.original: לָ֥מָּה תָרִ֖יבוּ אֵלָ֑י כֻּלְּכֶ֛ם פְּשַׁעְתֶּ֥ם בִּ֖י נְאֻם־ יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: “I have struck your sons in vain; they accepted no discipline. Your own sword has devoured your prophets like a voracious lion.”
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the people of Judah.
God says, “I punished your sons.
My punishment was in vain.
Your sons did not accept discipline.
You used your own sword.
Your sword killed your prophets.
Your sword destroyed them like a hungry lion.”
passages.original: לַשָּׁוְא֙ הִכֵּ֣יתִי אֶת־ בְּנֵיכֶ֔ם מוּסָ֖ר לֹ֣א לָקָ֑חוּ אָכְלָ֧ה חַרְבְּכֶ֛ם נְבִֽיאֵיכֶ֖ם כְּאַרְיֵ֥ה מַשְׁחִֽית׃

passages.text: You people of this generation, consider the word of the LORD: “Have I been a wilderness to Israel or a land of dense darkness? Why do My people say, ‘We are free to roam; we will come to You no more’?
passages.sermon:
This message is from the LORD.
The LORD speaks to the people of this generation.
He says, "Listen to My word."
He asks, "Have I been a wilderness to Israel?"
He asks, "Have I been a land of deep darkness to Israel?"
He says, "My people say, 'We are free to wander.'"
He says, "My people say, 'We will not come to You again.'"
The LORD questions why His people speak this way.
passages.original: הַדּ֗וֹר אַתֶּם֙ רְא֣וּ דְבַר־ יְהוָ֔ה הֲמִדְבָּ֤ר הָיִ֙יתִי֙ לְיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אִ֛ם אֶ֥רֶץ מַאְפֵּ֖לְיָ֑ה מַדּ֜וּעַ אָמְר֤וּ עַמִּי֙ רַ֔דְנוּ לֽוֹא־ נָב֥וֹא ע֖וֹד אֵלֶֽיךָ׃

passages.text: Does a maiden forget her jewelry or a bride her wedding sash? Yet My people have forgotten Me for days without number.
passages.sermon:
A young woman does not forget her jewelry.
A bride does not forget her wedding sash.
But My people have forgotten Me.
They have forgotten Me for countless days.
passages.original: הֲתִשְׁכַּ֤ח בְּתוּלָה֙ עֶדְיָ֔הּ כַּלָּ֖ה קִשֻּׁרֶ֑יהָ וְעַמִּ֣י שְׁכֵח֔וּנִי יָמִ֖ים אֵ֥ין מִסְפָּֽר׃

passages.text: How skillfully you pursue love! Even the most immoral of women could learn from your ways.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to His people Israel.
God sees that you try very hard to find love.
You use great skill to chase after love.
You do this with much effort and planning.
You act in ways that even the worst women could learn from.
You teach evil women new ways to sin.
Your actions go beyond what is common.
You show others how to do wrong by your example.
passages.original: מַה־ תֵּיטִ֥בִי דַּרְכֵּ֖ךְ לְבַקֵּ֣שׁ אַהֲבָ֑ה לָכֵן֙ גַּ֣ם אֶת־ הָרָע֔וֹת לִמַּדְתִּי אֶת־ דְּרָכָֽיִךְ׃

passages.text: Moreover, your skirts are stained with the blood of the innocent poor, though you did not find them breaking in. But in spite of all these things you say, ‘I am innocent. Surely His anger will turn from me.’ Behold, I will judge you, because you say, ‘I have not sinned.’
passages.sermon:
God speaks to His people Israel.
He says their skirts are stained with blood.
This blood belongs to poor and innocent people.
They did not find these people breaking in.
Still, the people say, "I am innocent."
They believe God's anger will turn away from them.
God says, "I will judge you."
He will judge them because they say, "I have not sinned."
passages.original: גַּ֤ם בִּכְנָפַ֙יִךְ֙ נִמְצְא֔וּ דַּ֛ם נַפְשׁ֥וֹת אֶבְיוֹנִ֖ים נְקִיִּ֑ים לֹֽא־ בַמַּחְתֶּ֥רֶת מְצָאתִ֖ים כִּ֥י עַל־ כָּל־ אֵֽלֶּה׃ וַתֹּֽאמְרִי֙ כִּ֣י נִקֵּ֔יתִי אַ֛ךְ שָׁ֥ב אַפּ֖וֹ מִמֶּ֑נִּי הִנְנִי֙ נִשְׁפָּ֣ט אוֹתָ֔ךְ עַל־ אָמְרֵ֖ךְ לֹ֥א חָטָֽאתִי׃

passages.text: How unstable you are, constantly changing your ways! You will be disappointed by Egypt just as you were by Assyria.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to His people Israel.
Israel acts unstable.
Israel keeps changing her ways.
Israel does not remain faithful.
Israel looks for help from other nations.
Israel will be disappointed by Egypt.
Israel was already disappointed by Assyria.
Israel will not find help from these nations.
passages.original: מַה־ תֵּזְלִ֥י מְאֹ֖ד לְשַׁנּ֣וֹת אֶת־ דַּרְכֵּ֑ךְ גַּ֤ם מִמִּצְרַ֙יִם֙ תֵּב֔וֹשִׁי כַּאֲשֶׁר־ בֹּ֖שְׁתְּ מֵאַשּֽׁוּר׃

passages.text: Moreover, you will leave that place with your hands on your head, for the LORD has rejected those you trust; you will not prosper by their help.”
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the people of Judah.
God sees that they trust in other nations instead of Him.
God says, “You will leave this place.
You will put your hands on your head in sorrow.
The LORD has rejected those you trust.
You will not succeed with their help.”
passages.original: גַּ֣ם מֵאֵ֥ת זֶה֙ תֵּֽצְאִ֔י וְיָדַ֖יִךְ עַל־ רֹאשֵׁ֑ךְ כִּֽי־ מָאַ֤ס יְהֹוָה֙ בְּמִבְטַחַ֔יִךְ וְלֹ֥א תַצְלִ֖יחִי לָהֶֽם׃
